preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 500000 for x in stdin.split()[:3])
preconditions.description: The first three integers n, m, q satisfy 1 ≤ n, m, q ≤ 500,000.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()[3:3+n]) == n and all(1 <= int(x) <= m for x in stdin.split()[3:3+n])
preconditions.description: The next n integers a₁, ..., aₙ satisfy 1 ≤ aᵢ ≤ m for each i.

preconditions.expression: all(n + 1 <= int(x) <= 10**18 for x in stdin.split()[3+n:])
preconditions.description: Each of the next q integers kᵢ satisfies n + 1 ≤ kᵢ ≤ 10¹⁸.
The input has exactly q + 1 lines (one for n, m, q; one for a₁..aₙ; and q lines for kᵢ).

postconditions.expression: stdout.count('\n') == q and all(1 <= int(x) <= m for x in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q integers, each between 1 and m inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split()) == q and (stdout.split()[i] == str(city_for_year(kᵢ, n, m, a)) for i, kᵢ in enumerate([int(x) for x in stdin.split()[3+n:]])))
postconditions.description: For each query year kᵢ, the output city is the one selected by the rule: the city with the smallest number of prior hostings (from years 1 to kᵢ-1), and the smallest index among ties. The function city_for_year(k, n, m, a) computes this by: (1) initializing a count array of size m+1 to zero; (2) updating counts for cities in a₁..aₙ; (3) for each year y from n+1 to k, selecting the city with the smallest count (and smallest index on ties), incrementing its count, and repeating; (4) returning the city for year k.
